title: The $10 Trap That Keeps You Broke
description: Every $10 you spend has two prices: what it costs today and what it could become. Learn how to think in opportunity cost.

segments.text: This ten-dollar purchase isn't costing you just ten dollars.
segments.visual_intent: A $10 bill is shown next to a small shopping bag. Text appears: "$10 ≠ Just Ten". No host gesture.

segments.text: Ask if buying this item today is better than letting that money sit idle, assuming it earns nothing.
segments.visual_intent: Reveal a single plain blank teal paper slip representing the alternative alongside one blank-screen phone. Renderer holds still; labels added separately by renderer.

segments.text: If that ten dollars earned an assumed eight percent a year for thirty years, it could grow to roughly one hundred one dollars.
segments.visual_intent: $10 → $22 → $47 → $101. A small graph grows upward. Text: “Compound growth”.

segments.text: Enjoy your coffee now, but ask if this optional spending is worth the future growth you are leaving behind by not investing it today.
segments.visual_intent: Renderer reveals an ordinary upright intact uncrossed coffee cup already still on the desk. Renderer holds this static illustration without internal transformation or hand motion.

segments.text: Weigh immediate pleasure against growing money over time by choosing to invest. Decide if buying now is worth what you give up.
segments.visual_intent: A balance scale appears showing fair comparison between alternatives, without an invented host pose or lettering baked into the image.

segments.text: Follow Wealth Blueprint and build wealth on purpose before you buy.
segments.visual_intent: Wealth Blueprint logo appears. Text: PRICE ≠ COST / Think in opportunity cost.
segments.on_screen: PRICE ≠ COST / THINK IN OPPORTUNITY COST

claims.assumptions: One initial deposit of 10 dollars, no recurring deposits, 30 years at an assumed 8 percent annual rate. Annual compounding; not a forecast; before fees, tax and inflation.
